rationale: The assistant immediately issued a correct stop-use/unplug instruction with the right warning about never opening the casing, asked the ideal first check (the right-wall panel for scorching), and correctly identified the 'cardboard-like panel' as a burnt waveguide cover. However, having reached the correct cause, it over-escalated to 'Panasonic support or a local authorised repair service' instead of advising the acceptable DIY fix of replacing the clip-on mica cover (model known, customer willing to buy a part) and cleaning the cavity, with engineer only if sparking persists. The hedged mention that the magnetron 'may' have been damaged is speculative but not a confident unsupported claim. Safe and accurate, but leaves the homeowner paying for an engineer over a cheap, acceptable self-repair.
